description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Latvian Gambit. Take on e5 and refute the early ...f5.

drills.briefExplanation: 2.Nf3 f5 3.Nxe5! — take the pawn; Black's attack never gets started.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the Latvian 2...f5 — develop and know the refutation.
drills.explanation: The refutation of the Latvian is 3.Nxe5!: White simply takes the pawn, and Black's 'attack' collapses before it begins. After 3...Qf6 4.d4 White has the center, the extra pawn, and the safer king — the f5 advance only weakened Black's kingside. Against unsound gambits, taking the material is often the strongest move.
drills.name: Taking on e5

drills.briefExplanation: 2...f5 3.exf5 e4 4.d4! d5 — take, counter in the center, and meet the block.
drills.description: White to play. Black is threatening the Latvian 2...f5 — take, meet 3...e4 with 4.d4!, and face 4...d5.
drills.explanation: If White took on f5, the strong reply to 3...e4 is 4.d4! — counterattacking in the center rather than retreating the knight to its doom. The d-pawn challenges e4's support, opens lines for White's bishops, and turns Black's wedge into a weakness. Central counterplay is the universal solvent for flank gambits.
drills.name: The d4 Counter
